purpose: sqlite3 is a lightweight embedded SQL database library.

functions.sqlite3_result_int: `sqlite3_result_int()` sets the SQL function result to a 32-bit integer. Call it from a user-defined function with the `sqlite3_context*` and an `int`. It stores the value as an internal 64-bit integer type; the DB mutex must be held.
functions.sqlite3_memory_alarm: `sqlite3_memory_alarm` is a no-op stub here. It accepts a callback, user arg, and threshold, but ignores them and always returns `SQLITE_OK`. It does not install any alarm or trigger any behavior.
functions.sqlite3_get_autocommit: Returns whether a db handle is in autocommit mode: nonzero = on, 0 = off. Use it to check if a BEGIN started a transaction or if COMMIT/ROLLBACK restored autocommit. After certain errors, it can tell whether SQLite auto-rolled back.
functions.sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64: Sets/queries SQLite’s process-wide soft heap limit. Call with N>=0 to set, -1 to read current. It’s advisory: SQLite tries to stay under it by releasing cache pages, but may exceed it. If hard limit is set, soft is clamped to it; 0 disables.
functions.sqlite3_aggregate_count: `sqlite3_aggregate_count()` returns the number of rows seen by the current aggregate/window context (`p->pMem->n`). Use it only from an aggregate function’s `xFinal`/`xValue`/`xInverse` context. It just reports the count; it doesn’t modify state.
functions.sqlite3_value_pointer: Returns a pointer stored in a `sqlite3_value` only if it was created as a pointer value of matching type string `zPType`. Use it to retrieve app-defined pointers from SQL functions. Returns NULL if not a pointer, type mismatch, or `zPType==0`.
functions.sqlite3_declare_vtab: Used by a virtual table module’s xCreate/xConnect to declare its schema (column names/types). Call once per vtab context with a CREATE TABLE-like SQL string. Returns MISUSE if called outside vtab setup or more than once; parser errors/malloc failure propagate.
functions.sqlite3_column_table_name16: Returns the UTF-16 table name for result column N of a prepared statement. Use after `sqlite3_step()`/`sqlite3_column_count()`. It reports the source table for that output column when available; otherwise it returns NULL.
functions.sqlite3_set_authorizer: Registers a per-connection compile-time SQL authorizer. Set xAuth/pUserData; it replaces any prior authorizer, or pass NULL to disable. On install, prepared stmts are expired. Callback runs during prepare/reprepare, returning OK/IGNORE/DENY.
functions.sqlite3_result_error_nomem: Marks a SQL function result as an out-of-memory error. Call it from a user-defined function when allocation fails. It sets the result to NULL, flags `SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT`, and records an OOM fault on the DB.
functions.sqlite3_blob_read: `sqlite3_blob_read()` copies `N` bytes from an open `sqlite3_blob` into `Z` at `iOffset`. Use only with a valid, unclosed blob handle. Returns `SQLITE_OK` on success; `SQLITE_ERROR` for bad/negative args or out-of-range read, `SQLITE_ABORT` if the handle expired.
functions.sqlite3_errmsg: Returns the most recent error message for `db`. Use after a failed SQLite call. If `db` is NULL or misuse is detected, it returns a fixed error string; if OOM, returns `SQLITE_NOMEM`; otherwise it returns `pErr` text or a generic message for `errCode`.
functions.sqlite3_open_v2: `sqlite3_open_v2` opens/creates a database with explicit `flags` and optional VFS `zVfs`. Pass a filename and `sqlite3**` to receive the handle. It just forwards to `openDatabase`; return value is that call’s status code.
functions.sqlite3_str_length: `sqlite3_str_length()` returns the current character count in a `sqlite3_str` builder. Use it to query how much text has been accumulated so far. If `p` is `NULL`, it returns `0`.
functions.sqlite3_os_init: Initializes/registers the OS/VFS layer for SQLite. Call once at startup before using SQLite; it sets up the platform-specific VFS and file I/O methods. Returns 0 on success, nonzero on init failure.
functions.sqlite3_column_text: `sqlite3_column_text()` returns the UTF-8 text for column `i` in the current row of a prepared statement. Use it after `sqlite3_step()` yields a row. It converts the value to text if needed; on error/OOM it may return `NULL` and sets the statement error state.
functions.sqlite3_db_cacheflush: Flushes dirty pager-cache pages to disk during an open write txn, across all schemas. Use on `sqlite3*` to force a mid-transaction flush. If locks block a db, it skips it and may return `SQLITE_BUSY`; other errors return immediately.
functions.sqlite3_errstr: `sqlite3_errstr(rc)` returns a static, human-readable string for an SQLite result/error code. Use it to display/log error codes from SQLite APIs. It does not set `sqlite3_errmsg`, allocate memory, or require freeing. Unknown codes map to a generic message.
functions.sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2: Runs a WAL checkpoint on db `zDb` (or all attached WAL DBs if NULL). Modes: PASSIVE nonblocking; FULL/RESTART/TRUNCATE may wait on writer/readers, with TRUNCATE also shrinking the WAL. Outputs `pnLog/pnCkpt`, or -1 on error/non-WAL.
functions.sqlite3_mutex_notheld: `sqlite3_mutex_notheld()` is a debug/assertion helper to test whether a mutex is **not** held by the current thread. Use it only for internal checks. It returns true if `p==0` or the mutex implementation’s `xMutexNotheld(p)` says it isn’t held.
functions.sqlite3_value_text16: `sqlite3_value_text16()` returns a UTF-16 native-endian text pointer for a `sqlite3_value*`. Use it to read a value as text; SQLite may convert the value if needed. It returns the internal text representation, so it’s only valid while the value remains unchanged.
functions.sqlite3_column_name: Returns the result-column name for prepared SELECT stmt column N (0-based). Use after prepare, before finalize/reprepare; pointer stays valid until then or next name call. AS alias is returned; otherwise name is unspecified.
functions.sqlite3_bind_text64: Binds a text value to parameter `i` in `pStmt` with explicit 64-bit length and encoding. Use it for large strings or when you need to specify UTF-8/UTF-16 encoding. `SQLITE_UTF16` is normalized to native UTF-16. It delegates to `bindText`; `xDel` must not be `SQLITE_DYNAMIC`.
functions.sqlite3_filename_journal:
Returns the journal-file name stored in SQLite’s internal filename bundle. Pass a database filename; it normalizes it with `databaseName()`, then skips past the main DB and related names to the journal entry. It returns a pointer into internal storage, not a new string.
This crash is caused by misuse: do not call sqlite3_filename_journal() with NULL, arbitrary strings, or ordinary file paths. Pass only a valid filename object previously returned by sqlite3_create_filename(). Check the argument for NULL before calling, and only use the returned pointer while the owning filename object remains alive. After sqlite3_free_filename(), do not reuse it.
functions.sqlite3_prepare_v2:
`sqlite3_prepare_v2()` compiles UTF-8 SQL into a prepared statement, same as `sqlite3_prepare_v3()` with prepFlags=0. Pass db, SQL, length, and get `ppStmt`; `pzTail` points to unparsed SQL. On error, `*ppStmt` is NULL.
When preparing fuzz input, do not use nBytes=-1 unless zSql is guaranteed NUL-terminated. Pass the explicit buffer length instead, e.g. sqlite3_prepare_v2(db, sql_buf, (int)sql_len, &stmt, &tail), where sql_buf is valid for sql_len bytes; if you need C-string behavior, allocate sql_len+1 and append '\0'.
functions.sqlite3_db_status: `sqlite3_db_status()` reports runtime stats for one `sqlite3*` connection. Pass a `SQLITE_DBSTATUS_*` op; it writes current value to `pCur` and peak to `pHiwtr`. If `resetFlg` is true, the peak is reset to current. Returns `SQLITE_OK` or an error; misuse checks may return `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT`.
functions.sqlite3_result_error_toobig: `sqlite3_result_error_toobig()` is a helper for SQL functions/aggregates to report `SQLITE_TOOBIG`. Call it with the current `sqlite3_context*` when the result string/blob is too large. It marks the context as an error and sets the message `"string or blob too big"`.
functions.sqlite3_exec:
`sqlite3_exec()` is a convenience wrapper to run 0+ semicolon-separated UTF-8 SQL statements via prepare/step/finalize. Use it for simple execution; optional callback gets each row, NULL means ignore rows. Errors stop current and later statements; callback nonzero returns `SQLITE_ABORT`.
Misused: the second argument must point to a valid NUL-terminated SQL string for the duration of the call. Do not pass raw fuzzer bytes directly as (const char*)Data unless you first copy them into a Size+1 buffer and append '\0'. Alternatively, avoid sqlite3_exec for raw binary input.
functions.sqlite3_result_zeroblob64: Sets the SQL function result to a zero-filled BLOB of size `n` without allocating the bytes. Use in UDFs via `sqlite3_context*`. Returns `SQLITE_OK`, or `SQLITE_TOOBIG` if `n` exceeds `SQLITE_LIMIT_LENGTH`.
functions.sqlite3_status: `sqlite3_status()` reports SQLite runtime status counters. Pass a `SQLITE_STATUS_*` op; it fills `*pCurrent` and `*pHighwater`, and if `resetFlag` is true it resets the highwater after reading. Returns `SQLITE_OK` or an error; NULL outputs are misuse with API armor.
functions.sqlite3_compileoption_used: Checks whether SQLite was built with a given compile-time option. Pass the option name with or without `SQLITE_` prefix. Returns 1 if found, else 0. If `zOptName==0` and API armor is enabled, it returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_limit: `sqlite3_limit()` sets or queries a per-connection runtime limit. Pass `newVal<0` to read current value; otherwise it changes the limit and returns the old one. Values above compile-time `SQLITE_MAX_*` are clipped. Use it to constrain untrusted DBs.
functions.sqlite3_bind_parameter_name: Returns the Nth bind parameter’s name in a prepared stmt. Use 1-based index. Named params like `:x`, `@x`, `$x`, `?NNN` return that exact text; anonymous `?` or out-of-range return NULL. UTF-8 only.
functions.sqlite3_value_subtype: Returns an application-defined SQL value’s subtype. Use it inside SQL functions to read context set by `sqlite3_result_subtype()`. It returns the stored subtype if `MEM_Subtype` is set, otherwise 0.
functions.sqlite3_vfs_register: Registers a VFS in SQLite’s global VFS list. Call with a valid `sqlite3_vfs*`; returns init/misuse errors if needed. If `makeDflt!=0` or no VFS exists, it becomes first/default; otherwise it’s inserted after the current default.
functions.sqlite3_preupdate_hook: Registers/replaces a pre-update callback on `db` and returns the previous `pArg`. Use it to observe row INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE before they happen. Pass `NULL` to disable. It stores the callback/arg under the DB mutex.
functions.sqlite3_create_filename:
Design: build an internal VFS filename blob from db/journal/WAL names plus URI key/value pairs. Use only in VFS shims; pass non-NULL D/J/W, and 2*N non-NULL params. Returns malloc’d pointer or NULL; free with sqlite3_free_filename().
Use the returned pointer only as an opaque SQLite filename object for the filename/URI helper APIs. Keep and pass the original pointer returned by sqlite3_create_filename() to sqlite3_filename_database(), sqlite3_filename_journal(), and sqlite3_filename_wal(); do not treat derived sub-pointers as interchangeable filename objects. Free it only with sqlite3_free_filename().
functions.sqlite3_errmsg16: Returns the current DB error message as UTF-16. Use after an API call fails. If `db==NULL` it returns “out of memory”; if the handle is unsafe/misused, “bad parameter or other API misuse”; if malloc failed, also “out of memory”.
functions.sqlite3_str_append: Appends exactly `N` bytes from `zIn` to a `sqlite3_str` buffer. Use `N>=0`; `zIn` may be NULL only when `N==0`. It grows the buffer if needed; otherwise copies in place. If the object is already in error, behavior is limited by its error state.
functions.sqlite3_mprintf: `sqlite3_mprintf()` formats text like `printf()`, but allocates the result with `sqlite3_malloc64()`. Use it to build strings, then free with `sqlite3_free()`. Returns `NULL` on init or memory failure.
functions.sqlite3_create_collation16: Registers a UTF-16 collation named `zName`. It converts the name to UTF-8, then calls `createCollation`. Use it to define custom sort order via `xCompare`. Returns `SQLITE_MISUSE` for bad db/name, otherwise API result; mutex-protected.
functions.sqlite3_log: `sqlite3_log()` is for writing to SQLite’s configured error log (`SQLITE_CONFIG_LOG`). Intended mainly for extensions, not apps. Call with a non-NULL format string; if logging isn’t enabled, it does nothing. Message formatting uses varargs and may be truncated.
functions.sqlite3_mutex_free: `sqlite3_mutex_free()` releases a mutex object via the mutex subsystem’s `xMutexFree` method. Call it only on a valid `sqlite3_mutex*` obtained from SQLite’s mutex APIs. If `p` is NULL, it does nothing.
functions.sqlite3_result_error: `sqlite3_result_error()` sets the current SQL function’s result to an error. Call it from a user-defined function via `sqlite3_context*`. It marks `pCtx` as `SQLITE_ERROR` and stores the message string `z` (length `n`; if `n<0`, treat as C-string).
functions.sqlite3_open: `sqlite3_open()` is the simple constructor for a DB handle. It opens/creates the named database as UTF-8 with `READWRITE|CREATE` defaults, returns `SQLITE_OK` on success, and usually sets `*ppDb` even on error. Always call `sqlite3_close()` when done.
functions.sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint: `sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint(db,N)` sets a WAL hook to auto-checkpoint after COMMIT when WAL reaches `N` frames. `N<=0` disables it. It replaces any existing `sqlite3_wal_hook()`, and is itself replaced by later `sqlite3_wal_hook()` calls. Checkpoints are PASSIVE; default is 1000 pages.
functions.sqlite3_result_error_code: Sets the result error code for a user-defined SQL function. Call it on the function’s `sqlite3_context` to mark the result as an error. If `errCode` is 0, it stores `-1`; if the output is still NULL, it also sets the error message text from `sqlite3ErrStr(errCode)`.
functions.sqlite3_trace_v2: Registers/replaces a per-connection trace callback for events in `mTrace`. Pass `xTrace=NULL` or `mTrace=0` to disable. It stores `pArg`, overwrites any prior trace/profile hook, and returns `SQLITE_OK` (or `MISUSE` with API armor on bad db).
functions.sqlite3_str_reset: `sqlite3_str_reset()` clears a `sqlite3_str`/`StrAccum` buffer. It frees owned text if malloced, then resets length, allocation, and pointer to 0. Use it to discard accumulated string content before reusing the object.
functions.sqlite3_finalize: `sqlite3_finalize()` destroys a prepared statement and frees its resources. Call it after use, at any stage of execution/reset. NULL is a no-op. It returns `SQLITE_OK` unless the last step/eval failed, then that error code; using a finalized stmt is undefined.
functions.sqlite3_memory_highwater: Returns the peak memory used by SQLite since startup or since the last reset. Call with `resetFlag!=0` to reset the high-water mark; `0` just reports it. It uses `sqlite3_status64(SQLITE_STATUS_MEMORY_USED, ...)` and returns the max value.
functions.sqlite3_result_text16be: Sets a SQL function result to UTF-16BE text. Use inside a user-defined function via `sqlite3_context*`; `z` is the text, `n` is bytes (or -1 for NUL-terminated), `xDel` frees/owns the buffer. If allocation/encoding setup fails, an error result is set.
functions.sqlite3_hard_heap_limit64: Sets/queries SQLite’s hard heap cap. Call with `N>=0` to change the limit and get the prior value; call with `N<0` to just read it. If `N` lowers the cap, `alarmThreshold` is also lowered (or set if unset).
functions.sqlite3_preupdate_count: Returns the number of columns in the row being updated/deleted by the preupdate hook. Call it only from a preupdate callback with the `sqlite3*` db handle. If no preupdate context exists, it returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_blob_bytes: Returns the size in bytes of an open BLOB handle. Use only with a valid `sqlite3_blob*` from `sqlite3_blob_open()` that hasn’t been closed. If the handle is null or not open, it returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_stmt_status: Returns a stmt counter value. Use `op` to pick the `SQLITE_STMTSTATUS_*` metric; if `resetFlg` is nonzero, that counter is cleared after reading. `SQLITE_STMTSTATUS_MEMUSED` is special: it frees the stmt and returns bytes used.
functions.sqlite3_prepare: `sqlite3_prepare()` compiles the first SQL statement in `zSql` into a prepared statement. Use a valid open `db`, then `sqlite3_step()`/`sqlite3_finalize()`. `pzTail` gets unparsed text. On error or empty/comment input, `*ppStmt` is NULL. Legacy; prefer `sqlite3_prepare_v2()`.
functions.sqlite3_column_value: `sqlite3_column_value()` returns the current column as an `sqlite3_value*` without copying. It’s for read-only access to a result row. If the value is static, it’s marked ephemeral before return. After `columnMallocFailure()`, it returns that value object.
functions.sqlite3_result_blob: `sqlite3_result_blob()` is for xFunc/xFinal callbacks to return a BLOB result. Pass the data pointer and byte count; `xDel` controls ownership: `SQLITE_STATIC` no copy, `SQLITE_TRANSIENT` copy, or a custom destructor. `n` must be >= 0.
functions.sqlite3_sql: `sqlite3_sql()` returns the original UTF-8 SQL text used to prepare `pStmt` (only for `prepare_v2/v3` and 16-bit variants). Use it to inspect the statement text; it returns `NULL` if `pStmt` is `NULL`. The returned string is owned by SQLite and freed on finalize.
functions.sqlite3_uri_int64: Returns an int64 URI parameter from `zFilename`. Use it to read a named URI query value, with `bDflt` as fallback. If the parameter is missing or not a valid decimal/hex int64, it returns `bDflt`; otherwise the parsed value.
functions.sqlite3_global_recover: `sqlite3_global_recover()` is a no-op stub that always returns `SQLITE_OK`. Its design aim is likely a placeholder for global recovery, but in this source it does nothing. Call it like a normal SQLite API; it always succeeds and has no effect.
functions.sqlite3_result_int64: `sqlite3_result_int64()` sets the SQL function/aggregate result in `pCtx` to a 64-bit signed integer. Use it inside a user-defined function callback. It stores the value directly in the result memory; the DB mutex must be held.
functions.sqlite3_next_stmt: Returns the next prepared statement on `pDb`’s internal list. Pass `NULL` to get the first stmt; pass a stmt to get the one after it. Returns `NULL` when none remain. `pDb` must be a valid open connection.
functions.sqlite3_value_text: `sqlite3_value_text()` returns the UTF-8 text representation of a `sqlite3_value*`. Use it to read a value as text in user-defined functions/callbacks. It may convert from other types; if conversion fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.sqlite3_free: `sqlite3_free()` releases heap memory allocated by SQLite’s allocators. Pass it a pointer from SQLite malloc/realloc APIs; `NULL` is allowed and does nothing. It updates memory stats when enabled, then frees via the configured allocator.
functions.sqlite3_result_text16: `sqlite3_result_text16()` sets a user-defined function’s result to UTF-16 native text. Pass the context, text pointer, byte length (`-1` for NUL-terminated), and optional destructor. It stores the result or an error if invalid.
functions.sqlite3_value_dup: Makes a copy of an `sqlite3_value`. Use it when you need to keep a value beyond its original scope. Returns NULL for NULL input or OOM. The copy is protected; blobs/strings are made writable. Free with `sqlite3_value_free()`.
functions.sqlite3_uri_key: `sqlite3_uri_key()` returns the Nth URI query parameter name from a filename/URI. Pass a valid `zFilename` and 0-based `N`. It skips the base name, then walks key/value pairs; returns the key string or `0` if `zFilename` is null, `N<0`, or not enough keys.
functions.sqlite3_value_blob: Returns a BLOB pointer from a protected `sqlite3_value`. If value is BLOB/TEXT it may expand/convert and returns `p->z` (or NULL for empty/NULL/OOM). Otherwise it falls back to `sqlite3_value_text()`. Pointer may be invalidated by later value access.
functions.sqlite3_create_module: Registers a virtual table module on `db` under `zName`. Use it before creating/using vtabs of that module. `pAux` is passed to `xCreate`/`xConnect`. If `pModule==NULL`, it drops existing modules with that name.
functions.sqlite3_bind_parameter_index: Returns the 1-based index of a named SQL parameter in a prepared statement, for use with `sqlite3_bind_*()`. Pass the name in UTF-8. Returns 0 if no matching parameter exists.
functions.sqlite3_total_changes: Returns total rows inserted/updated/deleted on this connection since open. Use after DML to get cumulative count. Includes trigger and FK-action changes; excludes REPLACE, INSTEAD OF-trigger view changes, and other connections’ changes.
functions.sqlite3_expanded_sql: Returns a heap-allocated SQL string with bound parameters expanded for `pStmt`. Use on a prepared statement to inspect the full SQL; free the result with `sqlite3_free()`. Returns `NULL` if no SQL or if tracing is omitted.
functions.sqlite3_mutex_held: `sqlite3_mutex_held()` is a debug/assertion helper to check whether a mutex is currently held by the calling thread. Use it only for internal sanity checks, not for normal control flow. It returns true for `NULL`, otherwise delegates to the mutex backend’s `xMutexHeld`.
functions.sqlite3_value_frombind: `sqlite3_value_frombind()` tests whether a `sqlite3_value` came from a bound parameter. Pass a valid `sqlite3_value*`; it returns nonzero if `MEM_FromBind` is set, otherwise 0. It’s a read-only flag check, not a converter or setter.
functions.sqlite3_unlock_notify: Registers/cancels an unlock-notify callback for a blocked shared-cache connection after SQLITE_LOCKED. If no blocker exists, callback runs immediately. If deadlock is detected, returns SQLITE_LOCKED and registers nothing.
functions.sqlite3_total_changes64: `sqlite3_total_changes64(db)` returns the 64-bit total number of rows changed by INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on that connection since it was opened. Use it to query cumulative changes; it just reads `db->nTotalChange`. With API armor, an invalid/unsafe `db` returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus: `sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus()` reports per-loop scan metrics for a prepared statement: estimated vs. measured work. Use it on a compiled stmt, with `idx` selecting a loop and `SQLITE_SCANSTAT_*` choosing the metric. Returns nonzero if idx is invalid or stats are unavailable; `pOut` is unchanged.
functions.sqlite3_filename_wal:
`sqlite3_filename_wal()` returns the WAL file name derived from a database filename. Pass a DB filename (or name accepted by `sqlite3_filename_journal()`); it returns a pointer to the WAL-name string in the same internal buffer. If WAL is omitted, it returns `0`.
Call this only with a valid SQLite filename object such as the original result of sqlite3_create_filename() or a filename pointer supplied by SQLite/VFS in the expected context. Do not pass the result of sqlite3_filename_journal() (or other derived component pointers) into sqlite3_filename_wal(), because it expects the full encoded filename layout and may read past the allocation.
This crash is caused by misuse: do not call sqlite3_filename_wal() with NULL, arbitrary strings, or ordinary file paths. Pass only a valid filename object previously returned by sqlite3_create_filename(). Guard against NULL before invocation, and ensure the filename object has not been freed. Do not use the result after sqlite3_free_filename() is called on the owning filename.
functions.sqlite3_result_text: Sets a TEXT result for a user-defined SQL function in UTF-8. Pass the context, string, length, and optional destructor for `z` (`SQLITE_TRANSIENT`/`SQLITE_STATIC`-style). It delegates to `setResultStrOrError`, so errors are handled there.
functions.sqlite3_enable_load_extension: Enables/disables extension loading on a db. Call with `onoff=1` to allow, `0` to forbid. It sets both `sqlite3_load_extension()` and SQL `load_extension()`. Default is off; returns `SQLITE_OK`.
functions.sqlite3_stmt_readonly: `sqlite3_stmt_readonly()` tells whether a prepared statement makes any direct DB-file changes. Use it on a `sqlite3_stmt*` after prepare. Returns true for SELECT/BEGIN/COMMIT/ATTACH, false if it might write (e.g. UPDATE, BEGIN IMMEDIATE), even if it ends up no-op.
functions.sqlite3_db_mutex: Returns the mutex that serializes a `sqlite3*` connection in Serialized mode. Use it only to coordinate external access to that DB handle. In Single-thread or Multi-thread mode it returns `NULL`; with an invalid db and API armor, it returns `NULL` too.
functions.sqlite3_free_filename: `sqlite3_free_filename()` frees a filename string previously obtained from SQLite’s filename APIs. Pass the pointer returned by SQLite; if `p` is `NULL`, it does nothing. It adjusts to SQLite’s internal allocation before calling `sqlite3_free()`.
functions.sqlite3_mutex_try: `sqlite3_mutex_try()` is a non-blocking mutex acquire attempt. Pass a valid `sqlite3_mutex*`; it calls the configured mutex backend’s `xMutexTry`. If `p` is `NULL`, it returns `SQLITE_OK`. Behavior for locked/busy cases is backend-defined.
functions.sqlite3_result_subtype: Sets the subtype on an SQL function result. Use inside an application-defined function via `sqlite3_context*`. Only the low 8 bits are kept; higher bits are discarded. It marks the output with `MEM_Subtype`.
functions.sqlite3_column_database_name: Returns the attached DB name for result column N of a prepared SELECT. Use on a prepared stmt; N is 0-based. Returns original unaliased name, or NULL if the column is an expression/subquery, on OOM, or if metadata support is disabled.
functions.sqlite3_close_v2: `sqlite3_close_v2(db)` closes a database handle, like `sqlite3_close()`, but is designed to be safer when statements/blobs are still open. It returns the result of `sqlite3Close(db, 1)`, so behavior depends on whether the connection can be fully closed.
functions.sqlite3_snapshot_open: `sqlite3_snapshot_open()` starts/updates a read txn on schema `S` to historical snapshot `P`. Use only when not in autocommit, no active SELECTs if a read txn exists, and DB is WAL-capable. Returns `SQLITE_OK`; `SQLITE_ERROR_SNAPSHOT` if checkpointed away; `SQLITE_ERROR` for invalid state/snapshot.
functions.sqlite3_snapshot_free: `sqlite3_snapshot_free()` is the destructor for a `sqlite3_snapshot*`. Use it to release any snapshot you obtained when done, to avoid leaks. It simply frees the object; if `pSnapshot` is NULL, `sqlite3_free()` is a no-op. Available only with `SQLITE_ENABLE_SNAPSHOT`.
functions.sqlite3_str_appendall: `sqlite3_str_appendall()` appends the entire NUL-terminated string `zIn` to an `sqlite3_str` buffer. Use it when you want to add all of `zIn` without specifying a length. It behaves like `sqlite3_str_append(..., strlen(zIn))`; `zIn` must be a valid C string.
functions.sqlite3_result_value: `sqlite3_result_value()` sets a SQL function’s result from an existing `sqlite3_value`. Use it inside a user-defined function with a valid `sqlite3_context*`. It copies the value into the output; behavior is just a direct copy under the DB mutex.
functions.sqlite3_str_finish: Finalizes and destroys a `sqlite3_str` builder. Returns the built string allocated by `sqlite3_malloc64()`; free it with `sqlite3_free()`. Returns `NULL` if `p` is NULL, the OOM sentinel, an error occurred, or the result is empty.
functions.sqlite3_file_control: `sqlite3_file_control()` is a low-level hook to send a file-control opcode to a DB’s VFS/file layer. Use it with a db handle and db name (`main`, `temp`, or ATTACH name; `NULL` = main). Some opcodes are handled by SQLite itself and write results into `pArg`; unknown db name or xFileControl failure returns `SQLITE_ERROR`.
functions.sqlite3_prepare_v3: `sqlite3_prepare_v3()` prepares UTF-8 SQL into a `sqlite3_stmt*`, like `prepare_v2`, but adds `prepFlags` (`SQLITE_PREPARE_*`) to control preparation behavior. Use `ppStmt` for the compiled statement and `pzTail` to find any unparsed SQL. Returns an SQLite result code.
functions.sqlite3_reset: Resets a prepared statement to its start so it can be run again. Bindings stay unchanged; use `sqlite3_clear_bindings()` to clear them. Returns `SQLITE_OK` after `step()` gave `ROW/DONE` or never ran; otherwise returns the last error code.
functions.sqlite3_result_double: Sets the SQL function result to a REAL (double). Call it from a user-defined function with the context and value. It stores the double in the output register; behavior depends on SQLite’s memory handling, but it does not return a value itself.
functions.sqlite3_value_int64: `sqlite3_value_int64()` returns the 64-bit integer interpretation of a `sqlite3_value*`. Use it on a value passed to a function/callback to read it as `sqlite3_int64`. It converts the underlying SQLite value to integer form via `sqlite3VdbeIntValue()`.
functions.sqlite3_bind_blob: Binds a BLOB to the i-th parameter of a prepared statement. Use after `sqlite3_prepare_v2()` and before `sqlite3_step()`. `nData` is byte count; negative is misuse. `zData==NULL` acts like NULL bind. `xDel` controls ownership (`SQLITE_STATIC`, `SQLITE_TRANSIENT`, or custom).
functions.sqlite3_column_text16: Returns the iCol result column as UTF-16 text. Call it after stepping a prepared statement and before resetting/finalizing. It converts the column value to text if needed; on allocation failure it records an error and may return NULL.
functions.sqlite3_value_free: `sqlite3_value_free()` releases a `sqlite3_value*` previously allocated by SQLite. Use it when you no longer need the value object to avoid leaks. If passed `NULL`, it has no effect.
functions.sqlite3_value_nochange: `sqlite3_value_nochange()` tests whether a `sqlite3_value*` represents a “no-change” value: it returns nonzero only when both `MEM_Null` and `MEM_Zero` flags are set, else 0. Use it to detect unchanged UPDATE column values.
functions.sqlite3_mutex_alloc:
Allocates a SQLite mutex. `SQLITE_MUTEX_FAST/RECURSIVE` create a new dynamic mutex; other ids return static internal mutexes. It auto-initializes SQLite first, returns NULL on init/allocation failure. Use dynamic mutexes in apps; don’t free static ones.
Use sqlite3_mutex_alloc only with valid SQLite mutex semantics: dynamic types (SQLITE_MUTEX_FAST, SQLITE_MUTEX_RECURSIVE) may be allocated/freed per use, but static types (SQLITE_MUTEX_STATIC_*) are singleton internal mutexes that must not be treated as independent objects, must not be freed, and should not be fuzzed as arbitrary user-owned locks. Avoid allocating a dynamic mutex while the current thread already holds a non-recursive static mutex, especially SQLITE_MUTEX_STATIC_MEM, because internal allocation may re-enter that same mutex and trigger an assertion.
functions.sqlite3_prepare16_v2: Prepares a UTF-16 SQL string into a reusable `sqlite3_stmt*` using the “v2” prepare path. Pass `db`, SQL bytes in `zSql`, length, and get the statement in `ppStmt`; `pzTail` points to leftover SQL. Returns an SQLite result code; on error `*ppStmt` is NULL.
functions.sqlite3_update_hook: Registers a per-connection callback for row changes in rowid tables. Call it on `db`; it replaces any prior hook and returns the previous `pArg`. No callback for WITHOUT ROWID/system tables; don’t modify the DB from inside the hook.
functions.sqlite3_clear_bindings: Resets all bound parameters on a prepared statement to NULL. Use after binding if you want to reuse the stmt with no values; `sqlite3_reset()` alone does not clear bindings. It returns `SQLITE_OK` and marks the stmt expired if needed.
functions.sqlite3_column_bytes: Returns the byte length of the current result column’s text/blob value. Call it after `sqlite3_column_text()`/`blob()` on a valid column index. It uses the current converted value, may trigger malloc-failure handling, and returns the byte count.
functions.sqlite3_keyword_check: `sqlite3_keyword_check(zName,nName)` tests whether the `nName`-byte token `zName` is an SQLite keyword. Use it to decide if an identifier needs quoting. It returns nonzero if keyword, 0 otherwise. It does not validate SQL syntax or null-termination.
functions.sqlite3_blob_open: Opens an incremental I/O BLOB handle for a specific row/column in a named DB. Use `zDb` as schema name (`main`, `temp`, or attached name). `wrFlag!=0` enables read/write; 0 is read-only. Fails if db/table/col/row invalid, or RW is disallowed; `*ppBlob` is NULL on error.
functions.sqlite3_column_double: `sqlite3_column_double()` returns the value of column `iCol` from a prepared statement as a `double`. Use it after stepping to a row. It converts the stored value via SQLite’s type rules; on allocation failure it still returns the converted value, with the statement error flagged by `columnMallocFailure()`.
functions.sqlite3_bind_int: `sqlite3_bind_int()` binds a 32-bit integer value to a prepared statement parameter. Use it with a valid `sqlite3_stmt*` and 1-based parameter index. It returns whatever `sqlite3_bind_int64()` returns, so errors/success follow that function.
functions.sqlite3_trace: `sqlite3_trace()` installs/removes a legacy SQL-trace callback. Pass `xTrace` to get UTF-8 SQL text as statements start (and for triggers); pass `NULL` to clear it. It returns the previous `pArg`. Deprecated; use `sqlite3_trace_v2()`.
functions.sqlite3_wal_checkpoint: `sqlite3_wal_checkpoint(D,X)` is a backward-compatible convenience wrapper for `sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2(D,X,SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE,0,0)`. Use it to checkpoint WAL db `X` on connection `D`: copy WAL content into the db file and reset the WAL. Passive mode means it won’t force locks.
functions.sqlite3_column_name16: `sqlite3_column_name16()` returns the UTF-16 encoded name of column `N` in a prepared statement. Use it after preparing the statement, with `N` in range. It returns the column name pointer; behavior follows `columnName(...)` for invalid/out-of-range cases.
functions.sqlite3_preupdate_old: `sqlite3_preupdate_old()` is for use **inside a pre-update callback** on `DELETE`/`UPDATE` only. It returns the **old value** of column `iIdx` via `ppValue`. Use valid column indexes; PK mapping is handled. Returns `SQLITE_MISUSE` if called outside callback/for INSERT, `SQLITE_RANGE` if index is bad.
functions.sqlite3_table_column_metadata: It’s a schema-introspection API: given db/table/column, it returns declared type, collation, NOT NULL, PK, and AUTOINCREMENT flags. Pass NULL for any output you don’t need; zDbName may be NULL to search all DBs. Returns SQLITE_OK if found, SQLITE_ERROR if not; NULL column checks table existence.
functions.sqlite3_create_function_v2: Registers or replaces a SQL function on `db`. Use `xFunc` for scalar, or `xStep`+`xFinal` for aggregate. `pApp` is passed to callbacks; `xDestroy` runs when the function is deleted/replaced or DB closes.
functions.sqlite3_snprintf: `sqlite3_snprintf` is a varargs wrapper around `sqlite3_vsnprintf` for formatting into `zBuf` with a size limit `n`. Use it like `snprintf`: pass the buffer, its capacity, and a format string. It returns the buffer pointer after writing the formatted text.
functions.sqlite3_set_last_insert_rowid: Sets the connection’s `last_insert_rowid` value manually. Call it on a valid `sqlite3*` to make `sqlite3_last_insert_rowid(D)` return `R` without inserting. It just stores `R` under the DB mutex; invalid `db` is ignored under API armor.
functions.sqlite3_vsnprintf: Formats into `zBuf` using a `va_list`, like `vsnprintf`, always NUL-terminating if `n>0`. If `n<=0` it returns `zBuf` unchanged. With API armor, NULL `zBuf`/`zFormat` is misuse; it may set `zBuf[0]=0` and return `zBuf`.
functions.sqlite3_value_type: `sqlite3_value_type()` returns the current SQLite datatype of a `sqlite3_value` as one of `SQLITE_NULL/TEXT/INTEGER/FLOAT/BLOB`. Use it in scalar/aggregate functions to inspect an argument’s type; it reports the effective type from the value’s flags, not a conversion result.
functions.sqlite3_bind_text:
Binds a UTF-8 text value to parameter `i` in `pStmt`. Use it before `sqlite3_step()`. `nData` is the byte length; `-1` means NUL-terminated. `xDel` controls cleanup of `zData` after SQLite is done.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of sqlite3_bind_text. Do not pass nData=-1 unless zData points to a valid NUL-terminated C string. For fuzz/input buffers or arbitrary binary data, pass the exact buffer length explicitly (>=0), e.g. sqlite3_bind_text(stmt, idx, ptr, len, SQLITE_TRANSIENT). If the data may contain embedded NULs or is not textual, prefer sqlite3_bind_blob(stmt, idx, ptr, len, SQLITE_TRANSIENT). If you want to use -1, first copy the bytes into a new buffer of size len+1 and append a '\0' terminator before calling sqlite3_bind_text.
functions.sqlite3_changes64: `sqlite3_changes64(db)` returns the 64-bit count of rows changed by the most recent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on that connection (`db->nChange`). Use it after executing a statement. If API armor fails safety checks, it returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_preupdate_new: `sqlite3_preupdate_new()` returns the post-change value for column `iIdx` during a preupdate hook. Use it only when a preupdate is active and the op isn’t DELETE. It maps PK indexes for non-UPDATE ops; out-of-range gives `SQLITE_RANGE`, misuse gives `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT`.
functions.sqlite3_db_handle: Returns the `sqlite3*` connection that owns a prepared statement. Use it to get the DB handle from `sqlite3_stmt*`. If `pStmt` is NULL, it returns 0; otherwise it returns the statement’s `db` pointer.
functions.sqlite3_column_blob: Returns the current row’s column as a BLOB pointer. Use only after `sqlite3_step()` returns `SQLITE_ROW`; index is 0-based. Pointer stays valid until next step/reset/finalize or type conversion. Zero-length BLOB returns NULL; OOM also returns NULL, check `sqlite3_errcode()`.
functions.sqlite3_drop_modules: Removes virtual table modules from a db connection, keeping only names in `azNames` (NULL = remove all). Iterate a NULL-terminated string list. If DB is invalid, returns `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT`; otherwise `SQLITE_OK`.
functions.sqlite3_result_blob64: Sets a SQL function result to a BLOB up to 64-bit size. Call with the blob pointer, byte count, and optional destructor. If `n > 0x7fffffff`, it frees/handles the value via `xDel` and does not store it; otherwise it stores the blob result.
functions.sqlite3_backup_pagecount: Returns the total page count for an active backup. Call it with a valid `sqlite3_backup*` from `sqlite3_backup_init()`. If `p==0` and API armor is enabled, it returns 0; otherwise it returns `p->nPagecount`.
functions.sqlite3_collation_needed16: Registers a UTF-16 collation-needed callback for `db`. Use it to lazily create missing collations when SQLite encounters one. It replaces any prior collation-needed handler, stores `pCollNeededArg`, and returns `SQLITE_OK`; invalid `db` may yield `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT`.
functions.sqlite3_malloc64:
`sqlite3_malloc64(n)` allocates `n` bytes from SQLite’s heap, using a 64-bit size. Call it like `malloc`; free with SQLite’s matching deallocator. If SQLite init fails, it returns `0`; otherwise it returns the allocated pointer or `0` on allocation failure.
