functions.sqlite3_config: `sqlite3_config()` sets global SQLite options before init or after shutdown only; it’s not threadsafe. Use it to tune rare app needs. If called while SQLite is initialized/in use, it returns `SQLITE_MISUSE`; unknown/failed options return an error code.
functions.sqlite3_value_double: `sqlite3_value_double()` converts an SQL value to a C `double` and returns it. Pass a valid `sqlite3_value*` from SQLite APIs. It uses SQLite’s numeric conversion rules: numeric values are returned as real, text/blob are coerced if possible, otherwise 0.
functions.sqlite3_auto_extension: Registers a statically linked extension init callback to run on every new DB connection. Call it once per extension; duplicates are ignored. It first initializes SQLite, then adds the callback under a mutex, returning SQLITE_OK or SQLITE_NOMEM/other init error.
functions.sqlite3_sleep: `sqlite3_sleep(ms)` pauses the current thread for at least `ms` milliseconds via the default VFS `xSleep()`. Use it for short delays, not precise timing. It returns the sleep time requested/rounded by the OS; if no VFS exists, it returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_changes: Returns rows directly modified by the most recent INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on that connection. Use it after those statements; other SQL leaves it unchanged. It counts only direct table changes, not triggers/FK/REPLACE or view INSTEAD OF actions.
functions.sqlite3_os_end: `sqlite3_os_end()` is the OS-layer shutdown hook. It should be called when SQLite is ending to release/clear Unix VFS global state. Here it simply resets `unixBigLock` to 0 and always returns `SQLITE_OK`.
functions.sqlite3_bind_value: `sqlite3_bind_value()` binds an existing `sqlite3_value` to a prepared-statement parameter. Use it when you want to copy a value into `?`/`:name` without converting it yourself. It preserves type: int, float, blob/zeroblob, text, or NULL. Returns the bind result code.
functions.sqlite3_bind_zeroblob64: Binds a zero-filled BLOB of size `n` to parameter `i` in `pStmt`. Use it like `sqlite3_bind_zeroblob`, but with 64-bit size. Returns `SQLITE_TOOBIG` if `n` exceeds the connection’s length limit; otherwise forwards to `sqlite3_bind_zeroblob`.
functions.sqlite3_last_insert_rowid: Returns the connection’s cached last successful INSERT rowid. Use it after INSERTs on rowid tables; 0 if none. Not set by WITHOUT ROWID or failed INSERTs. Triggers/virtual tables may affect it; concurrent use on same connection is unpredictable.
functions.sqlite3_errcode: Returns the last error code for a DB handle. Use it after an sqlite3_* call fails to inspect the result. If db is NULL or mallocFailed, it returns SQLITE_NOMEM; if the handle is unsafe/misused, SQLITE_MISUSE.
functions.sqlite3_system_errno: Returns the OS-specific errno for the most recent I/O/open-file failure on a db handle. Use it after an error like `SQLITE_CANTOPEN` to inspect the underlying system cause. If `db` is NULL, it returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_overload_function: `sqlite3_overload_function()` ensures a global SQL function name/arity exists so a virtual table can override it via `xFindFunction`. If already present, it does nothing. Otherwise it creates a placeholder that always raises an error. Use it before relying on VT-specific overloads.
functions.sqlite3_free_table: Frees the memory returned by `sqlite3_get_table()`. Call it with the `char**` result pointer from that API. If `result` is NULL, it does nothing. It frees each allocated string, then the table array itself.
functions.sqlite3_vtab_collation: Used only in `xBestIndex()` to get the collation name for a specific `aConstraint[]` entry. Returns that constraint’s collation if known, else `BINARY`; returns `0` if `iCons` is out of range.
functions.sqlite3_progress_handler: Sets a per-connection progress callback for long-running `sqlite3_exec/step/get_table` work. Use `nOps>0` to enable; `xProgress` gets `pArg` periodically. Return nonzero to interrupt. `nOps<1` or `xProgress=NULL` disables it; one handler at a time.
functions.sqlite3_value_numeric_type: `sqlite3_value_numeric_type()` returns a value’s type, coercing TEXT to numeric if it looks like a number. Use it to inspect a `sqlite3_value*` after numeric affinity. Non-TEXT types are returned unchanged; TEXT may become INTEGER/REAL or stay TEXT.
functions.sqlite3_reset_auto_extension: `sqlite3_reset_auto_extension()` clears all extensions registered by `sqlite3_auto_extension()`. Call it to disable future automatic loading. It initializes SQLite if needed, then frees the list under the main mutex; if init fails, it does nothing.
functions.sqlite3_collation_needed: Registers a per-connection “collation needed” callback. Use it to lazily create missing collations when SQLite first needs one. It replaces any prior callback, stores your context arg, and returns SQLITE_OK (or MISUSE if the db handle is invalid).
functions.sqlite3_prepare16: `sqlite3_prepare16` prepares a UTF-16 SQL string into a statement. Pass `db`, SQL bytes in `zSql`, and `nByte` length; on success `*ppStmt` gets the compiled statement and `*pzTail` points to unparsed trailing SQL. Returns SQLite error code; on failure `*ppStmt` is null.
functions.sqlite3_preupdate_blobwrite: Returns the column index being changed by the current preupdate hook via incremental BLOB I/O. Call only inside a preupdate callback on the same `sqlite3*`. If no preupdate is active, it returns `-1`.
functions.sqlite3_backup_step: `sqlite3_backup_step()` copies up to `nPage` pages from source to destination. Call it repeatedly until it returns `SQLITE_DONE`; `SQLITE_OK` means more pages remain. It returns `SQLITE_BUSY` if the source is in a write txn, and `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT` for a null backup handle.
functions.sqlite3_value_text16le: `sqlite3_value_text16le()` returns the UTF-16LE text representation of a `sqlite3_value*`. Use it when you need the value as little-endian 16-bit text. It converts from other types if needed, or returns the existing text encoding.
functions.sqlite3_snapshot_recover: `sqlite3_snapshot_recover()` scans a WAL to make older valid snapshots usable by `sqlite3_snapshot_open()`. Use it on a WAL-mode db with no active read txn; it returns `SQLITE_OK` on success, else an error.
functions.sqlite3_vtab_nochange: `sqlite3_vtab_nochange()` is an optimization hint for virtual table `xColumn()`. Use it during UPDATE to detect columns not being changed; then you may skip expensive computation and even omit setting a result. In `xUpdate()`, `sqlite3_value_nochange()` will reflect that. It may still return false.
functions.sqlite3_initialize: `sqlite3_initialize()` is the library startup hook. Use it before any other SQLite API if autoinit may be disabled; otherwise `sqlite3_open()` etc. may call it for you. First/effective call initializes; later calls are harmless no-ops. Returns `SQLITE_OK` or an error.
functions.sqlite3_rollback_hook: Registers a rollback hook on `db`. Use it to set a callback and user arg; it returns the previous arg. It only stores the hook under mutex, and on misuse/safety failure returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_interrupt: `sqlite3_interrupt(db)` sets an interrupt flag to abort current/soon-started SQL on that connection. Use it for cancel/Ctrl-C, even from another thread. Running ops return `SQLITE_INTERRUPT`; explicit INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE txns roll back. No-op if nothing is running.
functions.sqlite3_backup_finish: `sqlite3_backup_finish(p)` ends a backup object and cleans up state. Call it after backup use, even on error. It detaches the backup, rolls back any open destination transaction, and releases related mutex/list links. If `p==0`, it returns `SQLITE_OK`.
functions.sqlite3_create_module_v2: Registers a virtual table module on `db`. Use `zName` as the module name, `p` for xCreate/xConnect/etc., and `pClientData` is passed to those callbacks. `xDestroy` is called when the module is unregistered/replaced. Returns `SQLITE_MISUSE` on bad `db`/`zName`.
functions.sqlite3_preupdate_depth: `sqlite3_preupdate_depth(db)` returns the trigger/foreign-key nesting depth for the current preupdate callback on `db`. Use it only inside a preupdate hook. If no preupdate is active, it returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_create_collation_v2: Registers/replaces a collating sequence for a DB connection. Use `xCompare` to compare text; `pArg` is passed to it. `xDestroy` is called when the collation is replaced or the connection closes. Returns SQLite result code; `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT` if `db`/`zName` invalid.
functions.sqlite3_vfs_unregister: Unregisters a VFS from SQLite’s global VFS list. Call it with a valid `sqlite3_vfs*`; it auto-initializes SQLite if needed, locks the main mutex, unlinks the VFS, and returns `SQLITE_OK` (or init error).
functions.sqlite3_value_bytes: `sqlite3_value_bytes()` returns the byte length of the SQL value in UTF-8 form. Use it on a `sqlite3_value*` after obtaining the value; it delegates to `sqlite3ValueBytes(..., SQLITE_UTF8)`. For non-text values, it returns the size of their current encoding/representation.
functions.sqlite3_aggregate_context: Allocates/returns per-aggregate state for xStep/xFinal. First call with nBytes creates zeroed storage (or NULL if nBytes<=0/OOM); later calls return same buffer, not resized. Freeing is automatic at query end; call from same thread.
functions.sqlite3_vtab_on_conflict: Returns the current ON CONFLICT policy for a virtual table’s xUpdate during INSERT/UPDATE. Call only from xUpdate; it maps the statement’s conflict mode to SQLITE_ROLLBACK/ABORT/FAIL/IGNORE/REPLACE. Outside valid use, behavior is misuse-protected.
functions.sqlite3_str_new: Creates a new dynamic string builder. Use it with `sqlite3_str_finish()` to avoid leaks. If OOM, returns a valid singleton that rejects appends, reports `SQLITE_NOMEM`, length 0, and `finish()` returns NULL. `db` sets max length limit.
functions.sqlite3_randomness: `sqlite3_randomness(N,P)` exposes SQLite’s PRNG for app use. Call it to fill `P` with `N` bytes; `P` may be NULL. First/empty use seeds from VFS xRandomness; later calls generate internally. Thread-safe via PRNG mutex.
functions.sqlite3_blob_write: `sqlite3_blob_write()` writes `n` bytes from `z` into an open writable BLOB at `iOffset`. Use only on a valid `sqlite3_blob*` from `sqlite3_blob_open()` with write access. It can’t grow the BLOB; out-of-range/negative args fail, expired handles return `SQLITE_ABORT`.
functions.sqlite3_vmprintf: Formats text like `printf` using a `va_list` and returns a newly allocated string. Use it inside variadic wrappers. If `zFormat` is NULL it returns 0; init failure also returns 0. Caller must free the result with `sqlite3_free()`.
functions.sqlite3_libversion_number: `sqlite3_libversion_number()` returns the SQLite library’s numeric version (`SQLITE_VERSION_NUMBER`). Use it to compare versions at runtime, e.g. to check feature availability. It takes no args, has no side effects, and always returns the compiled-in version number.
functions.sqlite3_strnicmp: Case-insensitive compare of up to N chars. Use it like `strcmp` for prefixes. Returns 0 if equal (or N chars matched), <0 if left<right, >0 if left>right. NULL: both NULL→0, left NULL→-1, right NULL→1.
functions.sqlite3_column_type: `sqlite3_column_type()` returns the SQLite datatype of column `iCol` in the current row of a prepared statement. Call it after `sqlite3_step()` yields a row. It reports the value’s type as stored/converted; if memory allocation fails, it records the failure and returns the type value.
functions.sqlite3_complete: `sqlite3_complete()` checks whether a UTF-8 SQL string *looks* like a complete statement: it returns 1 only if it ends with a real semicolon, ignoring trailing whitespace/comments, and not as a prefix of `CREATE TRIGGER`; 0 if incomplete, `SQLITE_NOMEM` on alloc failure. It does not validate SQL syntax.
functions.sqlite3_blob_close: `sqlite3_blob_close` releases an open BLOB handle. Pass a valid handle or NULL; NULL is a no-op. It always closes the handle, then finalizes the backing statement. If the handle was RW, closing may commit the txn; on commit error it returns that code.
functions.sqlite3_cancel_auto_extension: Unregisters a function previously added by `sqlite3_auto_extension()`. Call it with the same entry-point pointer. Returns 1 if removed, 0 if it wasn’t registered. Thread-safe via the main mutex when enabled.
functions.sqlite3_bind_int64: Binds a 64-bit integer to parameter `i` in prepared stmt `pStmt`. Call after `sqlite3_prepare*`; index is 1-based. It first clears any prior binding, then stores `iValue`. Returns `SQLITE_OK` on success, else an error code.
functions.sqlite3_data_count: Returns the number of columns in the current row of a prepared statement’s result set. Use it after `sqlite3_step()`: nonzero after `SQLITE_ROW`, 0 if no row/data, `SQLITE_DONE`, NULL stmt, or statements with no result set.
functions.sqlite3_column_bytes16: Returns the byte size of the current result column in UTF-16. Call after `sqlite3_step()` and after fetching the column value (`text16`/`blob`/etc.). It reports the current converted value size, and may trigger `columnMallocFailure()` if allocation/conversion fails.
functions.sqlite3_bind_parameter_count: Returns the highest parameter index in a prepared statement (`p->nVar`), or 0 if `pStmt` is NULL. Use it to know how many bind slots exist; with `?NNN`, gaps may exist, so it’s not always the count of unique parameters.
functions.sqlite3_msize: `sqlite3_msize()` returns the size of a heap allocation previously obtained from SQLite’s memory allocator. Use it only on SQLite heap pointers. It returns `0` for `NULL`; otherwise it calls the allocator’s `xSize` to report the block size.
functions.sqlite3_txn_state: Returns the txn state for schema `S` in `db`: `NONE`, `READ`, or `WRITE`; if `S==NULL`, it returns the highest state across all schemas. Invalid schema => `-1`. Use it to inspect current connection transaction status.
functions.sqlite3_vtab_config: `sqlite3_vtab_config()` lets a virtual table’s `xCreate`/`xConnect` configure its connection-specific flags. Use it only during those callbacks; otherwise behavior is undefined and this code returns `SQLITE_MISUSE`. Options set constraint support or risk flags (`INNOCUOUS`, `DIRECTONLY`).
functions.sqlite3_malloc: `sqlite3_malloc(n)` allocates SQLite-managed memory after auto-init. Use only for `n>0`; otherwise it returns `NULL`. On init failure it returns `NULL` too. Free only with `sqlite3_free()`.
functions.sqlite3_result_null: `sqlite3_result_null()` is a result-setter for scalar/aggregate UDFs. Call it with the current `sqlite3_context*` to make the SQL function return NULL. It simply marks the context’s output value as NULL; no extra conversion or error handling.
functions.sqlite3_result_text16le: Sets the SQL function result to UTF-16LE text. Pass the text buffer, byte length `n` (-1 for nul-terminated), and optional destructor `xDel`. It stores the value or records an error if allocation/encoding handling fails.
functions.sqlite3_database_file_object: `sqlite3_database_file_object()` is a VFS-only helper: given the filename passed to `xOpen()` for a rollback/WAL journal, it returns the `sqlite3_file*` for the main DB file. Use only with `SQLITE_OPEN_MAIN_JOURNAL` or `SQLITE_OPEN_WAL`; other use is undefined.
functions.sqlite3_column_table_name: Returns the table name for result column N in a prepared statement. Use after `sqlite3_prepare*` on a valid `sqlite3_stmt*`. If the column isn’t tied to a table or N is invalid, it returns `NULL`. The returned string is owned by SQLite.
functions.sqlite3_status64: Returns current and high-water stats for `op`. Use valid `op` and non-NULL `pCurrent`/`pHighwater`; on misuse it returns `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT`. If `resetFlag` is nonzero, it resets the high-water mark to the current value.
functions.sqlite3_create_function16: Registers a user-defined SQL function/aggregate using a UTF-16 function name. It converts the name to UTF-8, then calls `sqlite3CreateFunc`. Use it with a valid `db` and non-NULL name; bad args return `SQLITE_MISUSE`, and it propagates `sqlite3CreateFunc`/API exit errors.
functions.sqlite3_bind_pointer: Binds `pPtr` to SQL parameter `i` as a typed pointer (`zPTtype`) with optional destructor. Call after preparing a stmt; index is 1-based. On success it stores the pointer and releases the DB mutex. If binding fails, `xDestructor` is called if provided.
functions.sqlite3_context_db_handle: Returns the `sqlite3*` DB handle tied to the current SQL function context. Use it inside user-defined functions/aggregates to access the connection that registered them. It just returns `p->pOut->db`; with invalid/null context, the assert may fire.
functions.sqlite3_stmt_busy: Returns nonzero if a prepared stmt has been stepped, is still “running” (not finished with `SQLITE_DONE` and not `sqlite3_reset()`), else 0. `NULL` returns 0; invalid stmt ptr is undefined. Useful with `sqlite3_next_stmt()` to find stmts needing reset.
functions.sqlite3_snapshot_cmp: Compares 2 valid `sqlite3_snapshot` handles from the same DB/WAL era. It orders by WAL restart salt, then `mxFrame`: older=-1, same=0, newer=+1. Undefined if snapshots are from different DB files or from before the last WAL delete.
functions.sqlite3_filename_database: Design: VFS helper to map a core-passed db/journal/WAL filename to the main DB name. Use only with filenames from SQLite core or `sqlite3_db_filename()`. Otherwise behavior is undefined and may crash.
functions.sqlite3_backup_remaining: Returns the number of pages still to copy in an active backup. Use it only with a valid `sqlite3_backup*` from the backup API. If `p==0` and API armor is enabled, it returns 0 and flags misuse; otherwise it returns `p->nRemaining`.
functions.sqlite3_backup_init: `sqlite3_backup_init()` starts an online backup from source DB to destination DB. Use it with different source/dest connections, then call `sqlite3_backup_step()` repeatedly and `sqlite3_backup_finish()`. It fails if handles are invalid, same DB, or dest has an open transaction.
functions.sqlite3_get_table: Legacy convenience wrapper over `sqlite3_exec()` that runs semicolon-separated SQL and returns all results as a flat UTF-8 string table. Use `sqlite3_free_table()` to release it. On error, `pzErrMsg` may be set; `pnRow/pnColumn` are filled if provided.
functions.sqlite3_column_int64: `sqlite3_column_int64()` returns the value of column `iCol` from the current row as a 64-bit integer. Use it after `sqlite3_step()` yields a row. It converts the column value to int64 if needed; `columnMallocFailure()` records any allocation failure.
functions.sqlite3_soft_heap_limit: Deprecated compatibility wrapper for `sqlite3_soft_heap_limit64()`. Call it with a heap limit in bytes; negative values are treated as 0. It just forwards the value to the 64-bit API.
functions.sqlite3_mutex_leave: `sqlite3_mutex_leave()` releases a mutex previously obtained with `sqlite3_mutex_enter()`. Pass the same non-NULL `sqlite3_mutex*`; if `p` is NULL, it does nothing. It asserts a leave handler exists, then calls the configured mutex backend.
functions.sqlite3_deserialize: `sqlite3_deserialize()` replaces schema `S` with an in-memory DB built from buffer `P`. Use it on an idle connection; `szDb` is data size, `szBuf` is buffer size. Fails with `SQLITE_BUSY` if the DB is in a read txn/backup. Free/realloc behavior depends on flags.
functions.sqlite3_normalized_sql: Returns the normalized SQL text for a prepared statement, mainly for comparing statements independent of literals. Call it with a valid `sqlite3_stmt*`; if `pStmt` is NULL it returns NULL. It lazily computes/caches the result, or returns NULL if unavailable.
functions.sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus_reset: `sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus_reset()` zeros all `sqlite3_stmt_scanstatus()` event counters for a prepared statement. Use it on a valid `sqlite3_stmt*` to restart scan stats tracking. It only exists when SQLite is built with `SQLITE_ENABLE_STMT_SCANSTATUS`.
functions.sqlite3_open16: `sqlite3_open16` opens/creates a DB from a UTF-16 filename. `ppDb` is set to NULL on entry; on success it returns `SQLITE_OK` and a handle, and for an empty filename (`NULL`) it opens the temp DB. It auto-initializes SQLite and returns `SQLITE_NOMEM` on conversion/allocation failure.
functions.sqlite3_transfer_bindings: Transfers bound parameter values from one prepared statement to another. Use only when both `sqlite3_stmt*` have the same number of variables (`nVar`); otherwise it returns `SQLITE_ERROR`. If either stmt is expired, it is marked expired first.
functions.sqlite3_prepare16_v3: `sqlite3_prepare16_v3` prepares a UTF-16 SQL string into a compiled statement. It always adds `SQLITE_PREPARE_SAVESQL`, passes allowed `prepFlags`, and returns an error code. On success `*ppStmt` is set; `pzTail` points to unparsed SQL, if any.
functions.sqlite3_commit_hook: Registers a per-connection commit callback, replacing any prior one. Returns the previous pArg. Use it to observe commits; return 0 to allow commit, nonzero to force rollback. Don’t modify the DB in the callback; pass NULL to disable.
functions.sqlite3_bind_double: Binds a C `double` to a prepared statement parameter `?i`. Call with a valid stmt and 1-based index. It first clears any prior binding; on success it stores the double and returns `SQLITE_OK`, else an error code.
functions.sqlite3_keyword_count: Returns SQLite’s current keyword count (`SQLITE_N_KEYWORD`). Use it with `sqlite3_keyword_name()`/`check()` to detect reserved words and quote identifiers. Count can vary by build/options and SQLite version.
functions.sqlite3_column_origin_name16: Returns the UTF-16 origin column name for result column `N` in a prepared statement. Use it to inspect the underlying table column a result comes from. Returns `NULL` if unavailable or `N` is out of range/non-originated.
functions.sqlite3_compileoption_get: Returns the Nth SQLite compile-time option string. Use it to enumerate build options: call with 0..n-1. It returns a valid string for in-range N, and 0 for N<0 or N>=number of options.
functions.sqlite3_serialize: `sqlite3_serialize()` exports a DB schema as bytes. Use `zSchema` like `"main"`/`"temp"`; `piSize` gets the byte size. Normally it mallocs a copy you must free. With `SQLITE_SERIALIZE_NOCOPY`, it returns SQLite’s internal contiguous image or NULL if unavailable.
functions.sqlite3_stricmp: `sqlite3_stricmp()` compares two UTF-8 strings case-insensitively using SQLite’s identifier rules. Pass 2 C strings; `NULL` sorts before non-`NULL` (`NULL,NULL` => 0, left `NULL` => -1, right `NULL` => 1). Non-NULL strings are compared via SQLite’s internal case-folding.
functions.sqlite3_vfs_find: Finds a registered VFS by exact, case-sensitive UTF-8 name; NULL returns the default VFS. It auto-initializes SQLite, locks the VFS list if threadsafe, and returns NULL if no match.
functions.sqlite3_enable_shared_cache: Design: process-wide toggle for shared pager cache/schema across DB connections. Use before opening connections; affects only future opens, not existing ones. Returns SQLITE_OK here. Shared cache is disabled by default and generally discouraged.
functions.sqlite3_bind_null: `sqlite3_bind_null()` sets parameter `i` in a prepared statement to SQL NULL. Use it on a valid `sqlite3_stmt*` before stepping. It unbinds any prior value; returns `SQLITE_OK` on success, else an error code.
functions.sqlite3_db_filename: Returns the absolute filename for attached DB `zDbName` on connection `db`. Use it to inspect the opened file path; returns NULL if no such DB or if it’s TEMP/in-memory. Pointer is owned by the connection and valid until DETACH or close.
functions.sqlite3_column_database_name16: Returns the UTF-16 database name for result column N in a prepared statement. Use it after `sqlite3_step()` on a valid `sqlite3_stmt*`. It returns the schema name for that column, or NULL if N is out of range or unavailable.
functions.sqlite3_uri_boolean: `sqlite3_uri_boolean()` reads a boolean query parameter from a URI filename. Use it with a filename and parameter name; it returns the parsed boolean value, or `bDefault` if the parameter is absent. If present, it accepts SQLite boolean strings via `sqlite3GetBoolean()`.
functions.sqlite3_set_auxdata: `sqlite3_set_auxdata()` lets a user-defined SQL function cache per-argument auxiliary data for reuse on later calls in the same VM/op. Use it inside a function callback with arg index `N`; SQLite stores or replaces the cached value and calls `xDelete` when discarded.
functions.sqlite3_blob_reopen: Moves an existing `sqlite3_blob` handle to another row in the same table/column/db. Use it instead of close+open for speed. New row must exist and hold blob/text; otherwise it returns an error, invalidates the handle, and later ops return `SQLITE_ABORT`.
functions.sqlite3_strglob: `sqlite3_strglob(P,X)` checks whether `X` matches SQLite’s case-sensitive GLOB pattern `P`. Use it for in-memory string matching, not SQL execution. It returns `0` on match, nonzero on no match, like `sqlite3_stricmp()`.
functions.sqlite3_expired: `sqlite3_expired()` checks whether a prepared statement is expired. Pass an `sqlite3_stmt*`; it returns nonzero if the stmt is `NULL` or its internal `expired` flag is set, otherwise 0. It’s a status query, not a reset/reprepare call.
functions.sqlite3_memory_used: `sqlite3_memory_used()` reports current bytes outstanding from SQLite’s memory allocator (malloced, not freed), including SQLite’s own overhead. Use it for diagnostics/monitoring only. It just queries `SQLITE_STATUS_MEMORY_USED`; it doesn’t reset stats.
functions.sqlite3_bind_text16:
`sqlite3_bind_text16` binds a UTF-16 native-endian text value to parameter `i` in a prepared statement. Use `zData` and length `nData` (`-1` for nul-terminated). `xDel` controls ownership/freeing. It returns the result of the bind operation.
Yes—this crash is caused by misuse of sqlite3_bind_text16. Do not pass nData=-1 unless zData points to a valid NUL-terminated UTF-16 string with a full 2-byte terminator (0x00 0x00) and proper alignment/length semantics. For arbitrary fuzz/input buffers, always pass the exact byte length explicitly, ensure the byte count is even for UTF-16 data, and if needed copy the data into a separate buffer and append a UTF-16 terminator before using -1. Also avoid SQLITE_STATIC unless the referenced buffer remains valid and unchanged until the statement is finalized or rebound; otherwise use SQLITE_TRANSIENT or a suitable destructor.
functions.sqlite3_test_control: `sqlite3_test_control()` is a SQLite-only test hook for reading internal state and injecting faults. Use it only in test code, with an op code plus op-specific args. Behavior depends on the op; e.g. PRNG_SAVE/RESTORE save/restore RNG state, and it may be absent or change across builds/releases.
functions.sqlite3_column_count: Returns the number of columns in a prepared statement’s result set. Use it on a `sqlite3_stmt*` to tell whether a statement returns data: `0` for no result columns (e.g. UPDATE), >0 for SELECT-like statements. It does not guarantee any rows.
functions.sqlite3_get_auxdata: Returns cached aux data for the Nth arg of a user-defined SQL function. Use with `sqlite3_set_auxdata()` to reuse per-argument metadata across calls when the arg value/op matches; otherwise returns NULL. Same-thread only.
functions.sqlite3_libversion: `sqlite3_libversion()` returns the SQLite library version string. Use it to query the linked SQLite runtime version. It takes no args and just returns the internal `sqlite3_version` constant; no side effects or error cases.
functions.sqlite3_db_release_memory: Attempts to free as much heap memory as possible for one `sqlite3*` connection. Call it on a valid db handle; it locks the connection, shrinks each attached btree pager, then returns `SQLITE_OK`. If the handle is invalid and API armor is on, it returns `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT`.
functions.sqlite3_wal_hook: `sqlite3_wal_hook()` registers one WAL-commit callback per `sqlite3*`. It replaces any prior hook and returns the old `pArg`. The callback runs after a WAL commit and lock release; use it to inspect, write, or checkpoint. If WAL is omitted, it returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_bind_blob64: `sqlite3_bind_blob64` binds a BLOB value to prepared-statement parameter `i`. Pass the data pointer, 64-bit byte length, and optional destructor `xDel` for ownership. It delegates to `bindText(..., 0)`, so it stores binary data, not text.
functions.sqlite3_sourceid: `sqlite3_sourceid()` returns the SQLite source ID string (`SQLITE_SOURCE_ID`), identifying the exact build/version snapshot. Use it to query build provenance or compare SQLite versions at runtime. It always returns a constant NUL-terminated string.
functions.sqlite3_result_zeroblob: Sets the SQL function result to a zero-filled BLOB of size `n`. Use it in a user-defined function via the context. It stores a zero blob in the result register; no data buffer is copied.
functions.sqlite3_column_int: `sqlite3_column_int()` returns the value of column `iCol` from the current row of a prepared statement as an `int`. Use it after `sqlite3_step()` yields a row. It converts the column value to integer; if conversion/memory issues occur, it still returns an int and records malloc failure on the statement.
functions.sqlite3_realloc: `sqlite3_realloc(pOld,n)` resizes a prior SQLite allocation. Call it after `sqlite3_initialize()` is available; it auto-initializes unless omitted. If `n<0`, it becomes 0. On failure it returns `NULL`; otherwise a resized block (possibly moved).
functions.sqlite3_busy_handler: Registers one busy-handler per connection. Use it to handle SQLITE_BUSY: callback gets your arg and retry count; return 0 to stop and get SQLITE_BUSY, nonzero to retry. Setting it replaces any prior handler and clears busy_timeout.
functions.sqlite3_keyword_name: `sqlite3_keyword_name(i, &name, &len)` returns the i-th SQLite keyword text and length. Use `0 <= i < SQLITE_N_KEYWORD`; on success it fills both outputs and returns `SQLITE_OK`. Out-of-range `i` returns `SQLITE_ERROR`.
functions.sqlite3_value_int: `sqlite3_value_int()` returns the SQL value as a C `int` by converting the `sqlite3_value*` with SQLite’s internal integer conversion. Use it when you need an integer from a function argument or result value. Non-integers are coerced; out-of-range handling follows SQLite’s conversion rules.
functions.sqlite3_value_text16be: `sqlite3_value_text16be()` returns the value as UTF-16 big-endian text. Use it on a `sqlite3_value*` when a function needs text in that encoding. It converts the value if needed; if conversion fails, it returns `NULL`.
functions.sqlite3_bind_zeroblob: `sqlite3_bind_zeroblob()` binds parameter `i` to a zero-filled BLOB of size `n`. Use it like other bind APIs after preparing a statement. It first unbinds any prior value; on success it sets the placeholder to a zeroblob and returns `SQLITE_OK`, else an error code.
functions.sqlite3_complete16: Checks whether a UTF-16 SQL string is a complete statement. Use it on a null-terminated UTF-16 buffer; it converts to UTF-8 then calls `sqlite3_complete()`. Returns nonzero if complete, 0 if not, or 0 on OOM/error after masking to 8 bits.
functions.sqlite3_close: `sqlite3_close()` is the destructor for an `sqlite3*` connection. Use it after finalizing statements, closing BLOBs, and finishing backups. It returns `SQLITE_OK` on success, `SQLITE_BUSY` if resources remain open; `NULL` is a no-op.
functions.sqlite3_profile: Registers a profile callback for `db` that gets SQL text and execution time. Pass `xProfile` and `pArg`; it returns the previous `pArg`. Setting `xProfile` to NULL disables profiling. Misuse safety check may return 0.
functions.sqlite3_strlike: `sqlite3_strlike(P,X,E)` tests whether `X` matches SQL `LIKE` pattern `P` with escape `E` (`0` means no ESCAPE). It’s case-insensitive for ASCII, handles Unicode, and returns `0` on match, nonzero otherwise.
functions.sqlite3_step:
Evaluate a prepared stmt. Call after prepare_v2/v3 (or legacy) and loop: SQLITE_ROW = read columns, SQLITE_DONE = finished, SQLITE_BUSY = retry/rollback as appropriate, SQLITE_ERROR/MISUSE = stop. v2 returns more specific errors; schema changes may trigger reprepare.
The crash is not caused by incorrect direct invocation of sqlite3_step itself, but by stepping a statement that executes a misimplemented aggregate UDF. Ensure any statement passed to sqlite3_step only uses callbacks that follow SQLite’s contract: aggregate xStep functions must not call sqlite3_result_*(), and only xFinal may produce the aggregate result. Continue using sqlite3_step only on prepared statements returned by sqlite3_prepare_v2(), check return codes, and finalize/reset statements appropriately.
functions.sqlite3_result_error16: Sets an SQL function result to an error message encoded as native UTF-16. Use inside a user-defined function via `sqlite3_context*`. It marks the context as `SQLITE_ERROR` and stores the text (or `n<0` for NUL-terminated) as transient data.
functions.sqlite3_threadsafe: Returns the compile-time mutex setting: 0 if SQLite was built without mutexes, nonzero if mutexes/thread safety were enabled. Use it to verify the linked library’s build, not runtime mode; sqlite3_config() doesn’t change its result.
functions.sqlite3_str_appendf: `sqlite3_str_appendf()` appends formatted text to a dynamic `sqlite3_str` using SQLite’s printf engine. Use it after `sqlite3_str_new()`. It doesn’t return status; errors are stored in the object and checked later with `sqlite3_str_errcode()`.
functions.sqlite3_extended_result_codes: Enables/disables extended result codes on a `sqlite3*` handle. Call with `onoff!=0` to get full error codes, `0` to revert to basic codes. It just sets `db->errMask` and returns `SQLITE_OK` (or `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT` if the db handle is invalid).
functions.sqlite3_value_bytes16: `sqlite3_value_bytes16()` returns the size in bytes of the UTF-16 representation of a `sqlite3_value`. Use it after obtaining a value in a function/aggregate context. It converts as needed and caches the result; if the value is NULL, size is 0.
functions.sqlite3_create_window_function: Registers a custom window function on `db`. Use it with `xStep`/`xInverse` to maintain state, `xValue` for the current window result, and `xFinal` for finalization. It just forwards args to `createFunctionApi`; return value is that API’s result.
functions.sqlite3_str_errcode: Returns the current status of an `sqlite3_str` builder. Use it after building to check for errors: `SQLITE_OK`, `SQLITE_NOMEM`, or `SQLITE_TOOBIG`. If passed `NULL`, it returns `SQLITE_NOMEM`.
functions.sqlite3_create_collation: Registers a custom collation on a DB connection. Use `zName`, encoding, context, and compare callback; passing `NULL` deletes it. This wrapper just calls `sqlite3_create_collation_v2(..., xDestroy=0)`, so no destructor is run.
functions.sqlite3_load_extension: Loads a shared-library extension into a specific `sqlite3*` connection. Call it after enabling extension loading; `zProc==0` lets SQLite pick the init symbol. Returns `SQLITE_OK` or `SQLITE_ERROR`; on error `pzErrMsg` may get malloc’d text to free with `sqlite3_free()`.
functions.sqlite3_result_text64: Sets a SQL function result to a text blob with 64-bit length. Use in UDFs via `sqlite3_context*`. If `n > 0x7fffffff`, it won’t store the text and only runs `xDel`; otherwise it calls `setResultStrOrError`. `SQLITE_UTF16` is normalized to native UTF-16.
functions.sqlite3_db_readonly: `sqlite3_db_readonly(db,N)` checks whether attached database `N` on connection `db` is read-only. Use it with a valid db handle and database name. Returns `1` if read-only, `0` if writable, `-1` if `N` isn’t attached (or on misuse with API armor).
functions.sqlite3_stmt_isexplain: Returns a prepared statement’s EXPLAIN mode: 0 = ordinary or NULL, 1 = EXPLAIN, 2 = EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN. Use it on a prepared `sqlite3_stmt*` to detect statement type before stepping/executing.
functions.sqlite3_mutex_enter:
`sqlite3_mutex_enter()` acquires the given SQLite mutex via the configured mutex backend. Pass a valid `sqlite3_mutex*`; if `p` is `NULL`, it does nothing. It asserts `xMutexEnter` exists, then calls it.
Call sqlite3_mutex_enter only on a valid mutex pointer returned by sqlite3_mutex_alloc, and do not re-enter non-recursive mutexes. In particular, do not enter SQLITE_MUTEX_STATIC_* mutexes and then invoke operations that may allocate memory or otherwise cause SQLite internals to acquire the same static mutex again. If re-entrancy is required, use SQLITE_MUTEX_RECURSIVE instead of a non-recursive mutex type.
functions.sqlite3_uri_parameter: Design: read a URI filename’s query parameter, mainly for VFS/custom VFS. Use only with SQLite-provided filename pointers (xOpen, db_filename, create_filename); NULL F/P returns NULL. If P exists w/o value, returns "" ; absent => NULL.
functions.sqlite3_shutdown: `sqlite3_shutdown()` cleanly deinitializes SQLite’s global subsystems after `sqlite3_initialize()`. Call it when SQLite is no longer needed. It shuts down OS, pcache, malloc, and related state; if not initialized, it’s a no-op and returns `SQLITE_OK` unless setup fails.
functions.sqlite3_str_appendchar: `sqlite3_str_appendchar()` appends `N` copies of character `C` to a `sqlite3_str`. Use it to build text efficiently. If more space is needed, it enlarges the buffer; if enlargement fails, it returns without appending. If `N<=0`, nothing is added.
functions.sqlite3_busy_timeout: Sets the connection’s busy handler to wait/retry on lock contention. Use `ms > 0` to enable a default timeout; `ms <= 0` disables busy handling. It replaces any prior busy handler. On timeout, `sqlite3_step()` returns `SQLITE_BUSY`.
functions.sqlite3_column_origin_name: `sqlite3_column_origin_name()` returns the original table column name for result column `N` of a prepared statement, if available. Use it on a valid `sqlite3_stmt*` after preparing a query. It may return `NULL` when the origin name isn’t known.
functions.sqlite3_db_config: `sqlite3_db_config()` sets per-connection options. Use `op` to choose a config verb: e.g. `MAINDBNAME` sets `aDb[0].zDbSName`, `LOOKASIDE` calls `setupLookaside()`, others toggle flags. Returns `SQLITE_OK` on success.
functions.sqlite3_snapshot_get: Takes a WAL snapshot of schema `S` for later consistent reads. Use only with a non-autocommit db, no write txn, and after WAL has data. It may open a read txn automatically; on success returns `SQLITE_OK` and sets `*ppSnapshot`, else `SQLITE_ERROR`/`SQLITE_NOMEM`.
functions.sqlite3_str_vappendf: Appends formatted text to a `sqlite3_str` accumulator using a `va_list`. Use it like `vprintf` for `sqlite3_str`: pass the target buffer, format string, and args. It handles flags/width/precision, and appends to the existing string; invalid/overflow cases are handled by the accumulator state.
functions.sqlite3_thread_cleanup: `sqlite3_thread_cleanup()` is a no-op stub. It exists as an API hook for thread-related cleanup, but in this build it does nothing. Call it only if your code expects the symbol; it has no effect in any scenario.
functions.sqlite3_column_decltype16: `sqlite3_column_decltype16()` returns the declared type of result column N as UTF-16, using the prepared statement. Call it after preparing a SELECT. It reports the column’s declared type if known; otherwise it returns NULL.
functions.sqlite3_create_function: Registers or redefines a SQL function on one `sqlite3*` connection. Use `xFunc` for scalar, `xStep`+`xFinal` for aggregate, NULLs to delete. `nArg` sets arity, `enc` selects preferred text encoding.
functions.sqlite3_result_pointer: Sets a SQL function result to a typed pointer. Use inside a user-defined function to return `pPtr` with type tag `zPType` and optional destructor `xDestructor`. It clears any prior result first; if `pPtr` is NULL, the result becomes NULL/pointer value.
functions.sqlite3_release_memory: Attempts to free about `n` bytes of SQLite heap by dropping non-essential allocations (e.g. page cache). Returns bytes actually freed, which may differ. If `SQLITE_ENABLE_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT` is off, it does nothing and returns 0.
functions.sqlite3_user_data: Returns the `pUserData` pointer saved when the SQL function was registered. Use it inside a user-defined function via `sqlite3_context*` to access per-function app data. It just returns that stored pointer; requires the same thread and a valid context.
functions.sqlite3_column_decltype: `sqlite3_column_decltype()` returns the declared type name for the Nth result column of a prepared `SELECT` statement, but only when that column maps directly to a table column. For expressions/subqueries it returns `NULL`. Use it to inspect schema metadata, not runtime value types.
functions.sqlite3_str_value: Returns the current built string from `sqlite3_str` as a NUL-terminated `char*`. Use after appending text to read the buffer. If `p` is NULL or no chars were added (`nChar==0`), it returns `0`; otherwise it writes the terminator and returns `zText`.
functions.sqlite3_realloc64: `sqlite3_realloc64(pOld,n)` is the 64-bit size wrapper for realloc. It auto-initializes SQLite, then calls `sqlite3Realloc`. Use it to resize an existing allocation to `n` bytes. Returns the new pointer, or `0` on init/allocation failure.
functions.sqlite3_extended_errcode: Returns the connection’s last error code, including extended codes. Call it with a valid `sqlite3*` after an operation fails. If `db` is NULL or `mallocFailed`, it returns `SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT`; if the handle is invalid, `SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT`.
